```plato
//==
// # Matrices
//
// Sections, in order:
//  - Dense matrix members — the IMatrix, IAdditive and IScalable surface
//  - Sparse and banded matrix readings

library Matrices
{
    //==
    // # Dense matrix members — the IMatrix, IAdditive and IScalable surface
    //
    // The per-type bodies that make the concrete matrices of `matrices.types.plato`
    // genuine `IMatrix` implementations: the shape pair (RowCount, ColumnCount),
    // zero-based element access, and the element-wise IAdditive / IScalable
    // arithmetic. Without these the generated members throw, so the whole derived
    // surface in `numeric-structures.library.plato` (Trace, FrobeniusNorm,
    // Lerp, ...) is unreachable.
    //
    // Convention: see CONVENTIONS.md - Matrices. Rows are stored as vectors, so
    // element (r, c) is component c of row r, and `Row1` is row index 0. The rows
    // are themselves `IVector`s, so element-wise arithmetic is just the same
    // operation applied per row, and `ElementAt` bottoms out in `IVector.At`.
    //
    // `Add`, `Subtract`, `Multiply(scalar)` and `Divide(scalar)` for `Matrix3x2` and
    // `Matrix4x4` are NOT restated here — those two types carry their full
    // System.Numerics-compatible surface in `matrices-ops.library.plato`, and only
    // the members that file omits appear below.

    //==
    // # Matrix2x2

    // Two rows.
    RowCount(self: Matrix2x2): Integer => 2;
```
